([[Baltimore, Maryland]]) | college = [[Northwestern Wildcats men's basketball|Northwestern]] (2019–2020) | draft_year = 2020 | career_start = 2021 | years1 = 2021 | team1 = [[Hamburg Towers]] | years2 = [[2021–22 NBA G League season|2021–2022]] | team2 = [[Capital City Go-Go]] | years3 = [[2022–23 NBA G League season|2022]]–[[2023–24 NBA G League season|2024]] | team3 = [[Santa Cruz Warriors]] | years4 = {{nbay|2023|end}}–{{nbay|2025|end}} | team4 = [[Golden State Warriors]] | years5 = [[2023–24 NBA G League season|2024]]–[[2024–25 NBA G League season|2025]] | team5 = →Santa Cruz Warriors | years6 = {{nbay|2026|start}}–present | team6 = [[Phoenix Suns]] | years7 = [[2026–27 NBA G League season|2026]]–present | team7 = →[[Valley Suns]] | highlights = }} ''' Patrick Andrew Spencer''' (born July 4, 1996) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Phoenix Suns]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA), on a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Valley Suns]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played college [[lacrosse]] for the [[Loyola Greyhounds men's lacrosse|Loyola Greyhounds]], where he set the NCAA men's lacrosse record for career assists (231) and is considered one of the greatest college lacrosse players of all time.{{Cite web |title=How Pat Spencer, a college lacrosse record-holder, made the Golden State Warriors|url=https://www.ncaa.com/news/lacrosse-men/article/2025-05-01/how-pat-spencer-college-lacrosse-record-holder-made-golden-state-warriors |access-date=December 5, 2025|date=May 7, 2025 |website=ncaa.com}} He also played one year of [[college basketball]] for the [[Northwestern Wildcats men's basketball|Northwestern Wildcats]]. ==High school career== Spencer is from [[Davidsonville, Maryland]]. Spencer attended [[Boys' Latin School of Maryland]], where he played both lacrosse and basketball. He earned four varsity letters for basketball and lacrosse. He was a US Lacrosse High school All-American, and he played for the Under Armour Underclass All-American Team Baltimore in 2014. He scored 30 goals and had 30 assists as a junior, and 49 goals and 51 assists as a senior.{{Cite web |title=Pat Spencer - Men's Lacrosse |url=https://loyolagreyhounds.com/sports/mens-lacrosse/roster/pat-spencer/6358 |access-date=2022-12-19 |website=Loyola University Maryland Athletics |language=en}}. In basketball, as a senior, he averaged 14.3 points, 8.1 rebounds, 6.1 assists and 2.3 steals per game.{{Cite web |title=Northwestern basketball lands an unusual transfer – the nation's top lacrosse player, Pat Spencer |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/college/ct-spt-northwestern-transfer-lacrosse-20190613-story.html|first=Teddy|last=Greenstein|date=June 13, 2019 |access-date=October 2, 2022 |website=[[Chicago Tribune]]}} Prior to his junior year, Spencer grew from 5-foot-6 to 6-foot-2. {{Cite web |title=Pat Spencer: How a Late Bloomer Became an Evergreen Sensation |url=https://www.usalaxmagazine.com/college/men/pat-spencer-how-a-late-bloomer-became-an-evergreen-sensation |access-date=2022-12-19 |website=www.usalaxmagazine.com |language=en}} ==College career== ===Lacrosse=== During Spencer's four years at Loyola, the team compiled a record of 49 wins and 19 losses, with the 2016 squad compiling a 14–4 record and reaching the NCAA Final Four.{{ cite web | url=https://loyolagreyhounds.com/news/2016/5/28/North_Carolina_Ousts_Men_s_Lacrosse_From_NCAA_Semifinals.aspx | title=North Carolina Ousts Men's Lacrosse From NCAA Semifinals | date=May 28, 2016 | publisher=Loyola }} Spencer holds the College Lacrosse record for career assists with 231 assists, as well as the [[Patriot League]] record for career points with 380.{{cite news|url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2021/10/28/former-loyola-maryland-lacrosse-star-pat-spencer-one-step-closer-to-realizing-nba-dream-after-invite-to-wizards-g-league-training-camp/|title=Former Loyola Maryland lacrosse star Pat Spencer one step closer to realizing NBA dream after invite to Wizards G League training camp|work=[[The Baltimore Sun]]|first=Edward|last=Lee|date=October 28, 2021|access-date=October 2, 2022}} Spencer received the [[Lt. Raymond Enners Award]] as the [[USILA]] national player of the year and the [[Jack Turnbull Award]] as the nation's top attackman in 2019. Spencer also received the [[Tewaaraton Award]], regarded as the [[Heisman Trophy]] for NCAA DI lacrosse, as a senior.{{cite web |url=https://www.usalaxmagazine.com/college/men/pat-spencer-takes-home-tewaaraton-in-third-year-as-finalist|title=Pat Spencer Takes Home Tewaaraton in Third Year as Finalist|work=USA Lacrosse Magazine|first=Matt|last=DaSilva|date=May 30, 2019|access-date=October 2, 2022}} As a senior on attack he also ranked second on the [[NCAA_Division_I_men's_lacrosse_records#Points|all-time points]] list behind [[Lyle Thompson]].{{Cite web |title=Pat Spencer Takes Home Tewaaraton in Third Year as Finalist |url=https://www.usalaxmagazine.com/college/men/pat-spencer-takes-home-tewaaraton-in-third-year-as-finalist |access-date=2022-12-19 |website=www.usalaxmagazine.com |language=en}} He was a four-time All-American. At Loyola, his head coach was Charley Toomey. In his first two collegiate games he scored eight combined points in wins over Virginia and Johns Hopkins University. In 2016 he took league first-team honoree for rookie-of-the-year trophy. He graduated from Loyola with a Bachelor of Business Finance.{{Cite web |title=Loyola Maryland's Pat Spencer Receives 2019 Tewaaraton Award |url=https://patriotleague.org/news/2019/5/30/mens-lacrosse-loyola-marylands-pat-spencer-receives-2019-tewaaraton-award.aspx |access-date=2022-12-19 |website=patriotleague.org |date=May 30, 2019 |language=en}} In an interview hosted by Paul Carcaterra, an ESPN lacrosse game analyst and sideline reporter, Carcaterra talked to Pat Spencer about college lacrosse and his background in basketball. Paul asks, "How big of an impact has hoops had on your lacrosse career". Pat responded, "Definitely a big impact, I think any time you play another sport a lot of it translates over". Later in the video, when Paul and Pat were shooting hoops, Spencer added, "Basketball and lacrosse are very similar, in terms of spacing and trying to draw a guy and find your open teammates".{{cite AV media |title=Paul Carcaterra RELAXIN with Loyola All-American Pat Spencer |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gSG_kxO8EIk |language=en |access-date=2022-12-19}} Spencer was selected by the [[Utah Archers|Archers Lacrosse Club]] as the first overall pick in the [[2019 Premier Lacrosse League season|2019]] [[Premier Lacrosse League]] collegiate draft. He did not dress or practice with the team, opting instead to pursue a collegiate career in basketball upon graduating from [[Loyola University Maryland|Loyola]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/28830585/why-pat-spencer-one-best-lacrosse-players-country-chose-play-basketball-northwestern |title=Why Pat Spencer, one of the best lacrosse players in the country, chose to play basketball at Northwestern |first=Adam |last=Rittenberg |website=ESPN.com |date=March 5, 2020 |accessdate=March 5, 2020}} ===Basketball=== Spencer used his college graduate year eligibility to play basketball at [[Northwestern University]] in the [[2019–20 Northwestern Wildcats men's basketball team|2019–20 season]]. He averaged 10.4 points, 4.1 rebounds, and 3.9 assists per game. The season was cut short due to the onset of the [[COVID-19 pandemic]]. ==Professional basketball career== ===Hamburg Towers (2021)=== In April 2021, Spencer joined [[Hamburg Towers]] of the German [[Basketball Bundesliga]] for the rest of the [[2020–21 Basketball Bundesliga|2020–21 season]].{{cite web |title=Pat Spencer, Basketball Player, News, Stats - USbasket |url=https://basketball.usbasket.com/player/Pat-Spencer/522176 |website=Eurobasket LLC |access-date=8 February 2026 |url-access=subscription}} In eight games, he averaged 7.0 points, 3.0 rebounds and 1.1 assists per game. ===Capital City Go-Go (2021–2022)=== In October 2021, Spencer joined the [[Capital City Go-Go]] of the [[NBA G League]] for the [[2021–22 NBA G League season|2021–22 season]].{{cite web|title=GO-GO ANNOUNCE TRAINING CAMP ROSTER|url=https://capitalcity.gleague.nba.com/news/go-go-announce-training-camp-roster/|website=NBA.com|date=October 25, 2021|access-date=June 26, 2022}}{{cite web|first=Chase|last=Hughes|title=Lacrosse legend chasing NBA dream with Wizards' affiliate|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/washington/wizards/lacrosse-legend-pat-spencer-chasing-nba-dream-wizards-g-league-affiliate|work=[[NBC Sports]]|date=October 27, 2021|access-date=October 2, 2022 }} In 26 games, he averaged 6.0 points, 2.1 rebounds and 2.2 assists per game. Spencer played for the [[Washington Wizards]] during the [[2022 NBA Summer League]].{{cite web |title=Pat Spencer Player Profile, Golden State Warriors - RealGM |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Pat-Spencer/Summary/151771 |website=basketball.realgm.com |access-date=8 February 2026 |language=en}} ===Golden State / Santa Cruz Warriors (2022–2026)=== On July 25, 2022, Spencer signed an [[Exhibit 10]] contract with the [[Golden State Warriors]].{{cite news|first=Zach|last=Zafran|title=An all-time great lacrosse player will be in Warriors camp|url=https://www.sfgate.com/warriors/article/Warriors-sign-Pat-Spencer-lacrosse-legend-17328228.php|work=[[SFGate]]|date=July 25, 2022|access-date=October 2, 2022}} He was later waived on October 15. He subsequently joined the [[Santa Cruz Warriors]] for the [[2022–23 NBA G League season]].{{cite web|title=Santa Cruz Warriors Announce 2022 Training Camp Roster|url=https://santacruz.gleague.nba.com/news/santa-cruz-warriors-announce-2022-training-camp-roster/|website=NBA.com|date=October 24, 2022|access-date=October 24, 2022|archive-date=October 24, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221024231301/https://santacruz.gleague.nba.com/news/santa-cruz-warriors-announce-2022-training-camp-roster/|url-status=dead}} He appeared in just nine games for Santa Cruz, averaging 10.8 points, 6.1 rebounds and 4.8 assists per game. On November 29, 2023, Spencer rejoined Santa Cruz.{{cite web|title=2023-2024 Santa Cruz Warriors Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/dleague/teams/Santa-Cruz-Warriors/35/Transaction_History/2024|website=RealGM.com|access-date=December 3, 2023}} On February 22, 2024, he signed a [[two-way contract]] with Golden State.{{cite web|title=Warriors Sign Guard Pat Spencer to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-sign-guard-pat-spencer-to-two-way-contract-20240222|website=NBA.com|date=February 22, 2024|access-date=February 22, 2024}} He made his NBA debut three days later against the [[Denver Nuggets]].{{cite web |title=Pat Spencer Enjoyed NBA Debut But Has Much Bigger Goals: "It’s Just The First Step In The Journey" |url=https://glennclarkradio.com/2024/02/28/pat-spencer-enjoyed-nba-debut-but-has-much-bigger-goals-its-just-the-first-step-in-the-journey/ |website=glennclarkradio.com |access-date=7 March 2024}} He appeared in six games for Golden State to finish the [[2023–24 Golden State Warriors season|2023–24 season]], averaging 0.7 points, 0.7 rebounds, and 0.8 assists. In 45 games for Santa Cruz during the [[2023–24 NBA G League season]], he averaged 13.0 points, 5.0 rebounds, 3.8 assists and 1.1 steals per game. Spencer joined Golden State for the [[2024 NBA Summer League]]. He continued with the Warriors for the [[2024–25 Golden State Warriors season|2024–25 season]]. On January 10, 2025, he scored a season-high 17 points in a 108–96 loss to the [[Indiana Pacers]].{{cite news |title=Pacers 108-96 Warriors (Jan 10, 2025) Game Recap |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401705091 |access-date=8 February 2026 |work=ESPN |date=10 January 2025 |language=en}} On March 4, 2025, his two-way contract with the Warriors was converted into a standard NBA contract.{{cite web | last=Martin | first=Angelina | title=Warriors convert Spencer to standard NBA contract, sign Key to two-way | website=NBC Sports Bay Area & California | date=2025-03-04 | url=https://www.nbcsportsbayarea.com/nba/golden-state-warriors/pat-spencer-standard-contract-braxton-key-two-way/1831934/?amp=1 | access-date=2025-12-03}} In 47 games for Golden State in 2024–25, he averaged 2.9 points, 1.2 rebounds and 1.1 assists per game. He also appeared in six games for Santa Cruz, averaging 18.0 points, 6.5 rebounds, 6.0 assists and 2.2 steals per game. On September 29, 2025, Spencer signed a new two-way contract with the Warriors, ahead of the [[2025–26 Golden State Warriors season|2025–26 season]].{{cite web|title=Warriors Sign Pat Spencer to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/pat-spencer-signs-two-way-contract-20250929|website=NBA.com|date=September 29, 2025|access-date=September 29, 2025}} In early December 2025, he received increased playing time due to injuries to key players, including [[Stephen Curry]]. He responded by averaging 15.2 points and 5.4 assists during a five-game span. On December 6, he made his first career NBA start, posting 19 points and seven assists in a 99–94 win against the [[2025–26 Cleveland Cavaliers season|Cleveland Cavaliers]]. Following the game, head coach [[Steve Kerr]] stated in response to questions related to his first start that "his coach realized that Pat is that motherfucker", referencing Spencer's own comments made about himself during a game against the [[2025–26 Philadelphia 76ers season|Philadelphia 76ers]] two days earlier.{{Cite news |last=II |first=Marcus Thompson |date=2025-12-07 |title=Pat Spencer,
